_metadata.description: The scenario-to-plugin declaration is the single source of truth for what a scenario publishes, and readiness is derived from it rather than guessed.

requirements.title: When the ramp composes a package, it shall read the scenario's plugin declaration from the governed scenario manifest and fail closed when that declaration is absent or invalid.
requirements.description: The declaration names which skills a scenario publishes, which CLI surface each skill wraps, the entitlement tier, and any MCP server. Inferring publishable content from the filesystem would let an unreviewed file reach a registry, so an explicit, schema-validated declaration is the only accepted input.

requirements.title: The ramp should report each scenario's publish readiness as the set of unmet prerequisites and name the first prerequisite that blocks eligibility.
requirements.description: Readiness is the operator's entry point: it answers 'can this scenario publish, and if not, what is the one thing to fix.' A boolean would hide the remediation, so the report enumerates every prerequisite with its state and marks the blocking one.

requirements.title: If a scenario is not standalone-installable, then the ramp shall mark it ineligible, name standalone install as the blocking prerequisite, and refuse composition rather than deferring the failure to rehearsal.
requirements.description: Standalone install is the stated gating prerequisite for the skill-registries channel. A package for a capability that cannot install without the full Vrooli runtime is a trust violation, so ineligibility must be explicit, attributed, and enforced at composition rather than surfacing later as a rehearsal failure. The fleet readiness board (OT-P1-005) presents this verdict; the refusal itself is a viability invariant and does not depend on the board existing.
